what_we_dont_measure: Model training emissions — amortized across all inference but not attributed per request
Embodied carbon of GPU manufacturing and data center construction
Network transit between user, gateway, and inference host
Cooling water consumption (WUE) at upstream data centers
Data center energy overhead (PUE) — we use a flat global average
Inference batch effects — single-user vs batched inference can shift per-token energy ~45% per batch-size doubling
Cold-start vs warm-pool serving — first request after idle costs more energy than steady-state
Prompt caching and context caching — repeated context costs less than first-time context
Speculative decoding overhead — accepted vs rejected drafts have different energy profiles
Hidden / reasoning tokens — for reasoning models, internal token counts we cannot see
Provider-side efficiency optimizations — vendor model serving improvements we cannot independently verify
Actual data-center region — most upstream APIs do not expose this; we use a global default
Market-based vs location-based electricity accounting — providers' RECs / offsets / PPAs not reflected here
Variability in actual inference compute per request — we use a per-1k-token midpoint
calibration_note: v1 uses static per-model midpoints with a declared ±100% margin (single-value UI is for readability — actual real-world band is wider, especially for closed-provider models). v2 will integrate live ML-CO2 API + per-region grid factors + bands & confidence labels. Coefficients are reviewed quarterly. If a model is missing from this table, the badge shows '~?g' rather than guessing.
